Marker dot plot

Source: R/dot_plots.R
DotPlot_bioToolkit.Rd

Shows, for each gene and group of cells, the percentage of cells expressing the gene (dot size) and its mean expression (colour), scaled across groups by default. A drop-in alternative to Seurat::DotPlot() and SCpubr::do_DotPlot(), with gene groups, clustering, a coloured marker for each group, gene names in italics and a fixed size: every row and column is `cell.height` / `cell.width` inches, so dots and text are the same size in every figure. Save it with save_plot; the numbers behind it are returned by export_source_data.

Usage

DotPlot_bioToolkit(
  object,
  features,
  group.by = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  cells = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  slot = "data",
  average = c("linear", "log"),
  scale = TRUE,
  expr.threshold = 0,
  pct.min = 0,
  pct.max = 100,
  min.cutoff = NA,
  max.cutoff = NA,
  cluster.features = FALSE,
  cluster.groups = FALSE,
  cols = NULL,
  group.marker = c("dot", "strip", "none"),
  group.cols = NULL,
  feature.group.cols = NULL,
  feature.group.side = c("opposite", "labels"),
  split.by.cols = NULL,
  split.by.side = c("opposite", "labels"),
  group.bar.width = 3.5,
  flip = FALSE,
  italic.genes = TRUE,
  fill.title = NULL,
  size.title = "% expressing",
  cell.width = 0.18,
  cell.height = 0.18,
  legend.position = c("right", "left", "top", "bottom", "none"),
  bg = "transparent"
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object

features

Genes to plot: a character vector, or a named list of character vectors (e.g. markers per cell type, see top_markers), drawn as labelled groups of columns. Genes are matched exactly (rat and mouse symbols are e.g. "Cd3e", human "CD3E"); genes not in the assay are left out with a warning. A gene in two groups is drawn in both

group.by

Metadata column to group cells by: one row per group, marked by the group's colour (see `group.marker`). If NULL (default), the active identities

split.by

Metadata column of a higher-level grouping, drawn like facets: one labelled block of rows per level, each with one row per group. E.g. `group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type"` compares conditions within each cell type. Default is NULL. (Seurat's `split.by` is the other way round: it splits each group)

cells

Cells to use, as names or indices. If NULL (default), all

assay

Assay to read expression from. If NULL (default), the default assay of the object, as in Seurat and SCpubr. The assay and layer used are always reported in a message and written to the source data. Set it explicitly when the object holds several assays (e.g. "RNA" and "SCT"), which give different values for the same gene

slot

Layer to read, default is "data" (log-normalized values). For "data", see `average`; other layers are averaged as they are

average

How the mean expression of a group is computed from the log-normalized "data" layer:

"linear"

(default, as Seurat::DotPlot()) log1p(mean(expm1(x))): the log of the mean normalized expression, i.e. a pseudobulk of the group, on the scale of Seurat's fold changes

"log"

(as SCpubr::do_DotPlot()) mean(x): the mean of the log-normalized values, less influenced by a few cells with very high expression

scale

Whether to z-score each gene's mean expression across the plotted groups, default is TRUE (as Seurat; SCpubr's `zscore.data`). Scaled colours compare groups for each gene, not genes with each other. Needs at least two groups

expr.threshold

A cell expresses a gene when its value is above this, default is 0

pct.min

Dots of groups with fewer than this percentage of cells expressing the gene are not drawn (SCpubr's `dot.min`, which defaults to 5), default is 0. They still count for scaling and are kept in the source data

pct.max

Percentage drawn as the largest dot, default is 100. Lower it for genes detected in few cells (e.g. transcription factors); higher percentages are drawn at the largest size and the legend says so

min.cutoff, max.cutoff

Ends of the colour scale: a number, a quantile of the plotted values such as "q5" / "q95", or NA (default). With `scale = TRUE` the scale is centred on 0 and each end is the cutoff (NA: +-2.5) or, when closer to 0, the most extreme z-score on that side, so that it gets the full colour; otherwise 0 and the largest mean. Values beyond the ends get the colour of the end

cluster.features

Whether to order genes by hierarchical clustering of their colour values (within each group of `features`), default is FALSE

cluster.groups

Whether to order the groups by hierarchical clustering of their colour values, default is FALSE. With `split.by`, the groups are ordered the same way in every block, by their values in all blocks

cols

Colours of the expression scale. If NULL (default), "blue-magenta" (diverging) with `scale = TRUE`, else "viridis_r" (sequential, yellow to dark purple). Otherwise a palette name (see show_palettes) or colours from low to high, e.g. `c("grey90", "darkred")` or `c(low, mid, high)`

group.marker

How each group is marked with its colour next to its label: "dot" (default; a coloured dot), "strip" (a colour strip) or "none"

group.cols

Colours of the group markers: NULL (default) for the colours DimPlot_bioToolkit gives them ("scanpy-20" up to 20 groups), a qualitative palette name, or colours named by group (or in level order)

feature.group.cols

Colours of the bars marking the groups of genes (a named list of `features`): NULL (default) for black bars, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by gene group

feature.group.side

Side of the gene groups: "opposite" (default; opposite the gene names: on top, or on the right with `flip = TRUE`) or "labels" (beyond the gene names)

split.by.cols

Colours of the bars marking the `split.by` blocks: NULL (default) for black bars, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by level of `split.by`

split.by.side

Side of the `split.by` blocks: "opposite" (default; opposite the group names: on the right, or on top with `flip = TRUE`) or "labels" (beyond the group names)

group.bar.width

Thickness of the bars marking gene groups and `split.by` blocks, in points, default is 3.5

flip

Whether to draw genes as rows and groups as columns, default is FALSE (genes as columns, as Seurat)

italic.genes

Whether gene names are set in italics, default is TRUE. Set FALSE for features that are not genes (e.g. proteins of an ADT assay)

fill.title

Title of the colour legend. If NULL (default), "Mean expression", with "(z-score)" when scaled

size.title

Title of the size legend, default is "% expressing"

cell.width, cell.height

Width of a column and height of a row in inches, default is 0.18 (13 pt). Dots scale with them

legend.position

Position of the legends: "right" (default), "left", "top", "bottom" or "none"

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

Value

A ggplot object

Details

Cells without a value of `group.by` (or `split.by`) are left out, with a message. Groups (and group-split combinations) with no cells are not drawn; group colours are still taken from all levels of `group.by` in the whole object, so that they match an embedding of all cells.

The source data (export_source_data) hold one row per group (and split) and gene: the number of cells, `pct_expressing`, `mean_expression`, `mean_expression_scaled` (when scaled), whether the dot is `drawn`, and the `assay`, `layer` and `average` used.

See also

top_markers, FeaturePlot_bioToolkit, save_plot, export_source_data

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Genes as a vector, from the SCT assay
DotPlot_bioToolkit(obj, features = c("Cd3e", "Ms4a1", "Cd68"),
                   group.by = "cell_type", assay = "SCT")

# Marker sets per cell type, drawn as labelled groups of columns
markers <- list(
    "T cells" = c("Cd3e", "Cd3d"),
    "B cells" = c("Ms4a1", "Cd79a"),
    "Macrophages" = c("Cd68", "Lyz2")
)
p <- DotPlot_bioToolkit(obj, features = markers, group.by = "cell_type")
save_plot(p, "dotplot.pdf")

# As SCpubr::do_DotPlot(): mean of log values, unscaled, dots from 5\
DotPlot_bioToolkit(obj, features = markers, group.by = "cell_type",
                   average = "log", scale = FALSE, pct.min = 5)

# Top markers from FindAllMarkers()
all_markers <- Seurat::FindAllMarkers(obj, only.pos = TRUE)
DotPlot_bioToolkit(obj, features = top_markers(all_markers, n = 3))
} # }
